title: Python: PEP 695 type parameters bind no name; a type-parameter name shadows nothing today (follow-up from GCLI-111 R4 review N5)
description: Found in the GCLI-111 round 2 review (N5), pre-existing and shared with rule 6d, not an R4 regression. A PEP 695 type parameter (def h[x](): x.run(), class K[x]: ..., type A[x] = ...) binds x in the generic's own annotation scope, but the walker records no binding for it. With x also bound in an enclosing function as C(), x.run() inside h resolves to C.run, though at runtime x is the type parameter. Fix in the walker (record the type-parameter names as bindings of the scope they shadow in, or refuse a name that a type parameter list declares), with a refused fixture per form (function, class, type alias, bounded, constrained, TypeVarTuple and ParamSpec spellings) and a positive twin, and a five-pin corpus diff that names any site that moves for 6d, R4, K1, LIT and M1. Not part of the DEC-303 build order; filed as a follow-up. DEC-303 (a22) item 2: a target is admitted when every binding of the name can be enumerated from the text of its scope.

acceptanceCriteria.text: a name declared by a PEP 695 type parameter list is not read as the enclosing scope binding by 6d, R4, K1, LIT or M1, with a refused fixture per form that asserts no edge leaves the call site and the receiver bin, and a positive twin
a per-site five-pin corpus diff is recorded and any site that moves is named

implementationNotes: GCLI-112 built (no count measured first, per the leader's brief): a PEP 695 type-parameter list now gets its own scope (Scope.typeParams) between the enclosing scope and a generic def, class or type alias, binding each declared name as rebound, so a read of it refuses instead of reaching an enclosing binding. Forms: def, class, type alias (value walked in the alias's scope), bounded, constrained, TypeVarTuple, ParamSpec, a method of a generic class (class parameters stay visible to methods, which skip the class scope), a generic method, a nested def. A parameter annotation, a class base and its parentScope resolve through the type-parameter scope; defaults and decorators stay in the enclosing scope (decoratorScope and the nonlocal walk skip it). A list holding a parse error (the grammar rejects PEP 696 defaults) counts every identifier in it, a superset that only refuses more. Fixtures: 18 (describe GCLI-112): on origin/dev bdeaaa22 14 fail and 4 pass (the positive twins and non-shadow cases); on the fix all 18 pass. Mutants observed red: no names bound 14, def scope parent outer 9, class scope parent outer 2, annotation scope outer 1, base scope outer 1, alias value outer 1, parse-error superset dropped 1. Five-pin delta: delta.ts on the fix and on origin/dev, cmp IDENTICAL (the corpus has no PEP 695 syntax); equals the post-GCLI-121 edge list.

Round 1 (Opus, head 2cfe524a) BLOCK, fixed in the next commit. B1: the type-parameter scope hid an enclosing class body (lookupBindings skips a class that is not the first scope looked in), so a generic declared in a class body no longer read the class's names (annotation, base, alias value); fix: the class stays the first real scope while only type-parameter scopes precede it (first = first && current.typeParams), a generic method's own body still skips the class. Red fixtures on the 2cfe524a head before the fix, green after; they also pass on origin/dev, so the old behaviour is kept. B2: every per-form fixture now asserts the full refused delta (receiver 1). Taken: N1 (test title), N3 (class keyword arguments walk in the type-parameter scope), N4 (alias value by the right field); N2 left (the resolver reads decorators through parentScope, which only refuses more). Mutants red: no names 16, def scope parent outer 10, class scope parent outer 3, annotation scope 1, base scope 1, alias value 1, parse-error superset 1, first dropped 1. Five-pin cmp IDENTICAL to origin/dev; bun test 1162 pass.

Round 2 (Opus, head 2f6ca5ff) BLOCK, DEC-303 (a71) arm A applied: Rule 36(ii) no longer saw a bare call in a generic's annotation, return type, base, class keyword argument or alias value inside a class body (calls.ts:1213 tested frame.scope.kind === class, but those walk in the type-parameter scope, function-kind), so a def called bare in its class body kept a receiver. Fix: one helper withoutTypeParameterScopes (walks past leading typeParams scopes) used at the Rule 36(ii) test (calls.ts 1213) and at enumerableBindings' class-body test (3806), which also refuses a name found in a type-parameter scope. Sweep: 1483, 1549 and 1598 test a decorator or def frame scope, never a type-parameter scope (it holds only expressions), unchanged; lookupBindings already keeps the class first (round 1). Fixtures: ten new (describe: bare call in a generic's expression inside a class body), five red on 2f6ca5ff (alias value, parameter annotation, return type, class base, class keyword argument), the non-generic twins and body twin pass on both, plus a generic method's own body stays a non-use. Shadowed base half asserts its measured bin: external 1 (a rebound base is an external base, not an in-repo edge). Mutants red: eight of round 1 plus helper dropped at 1213 (5); the two enumerableBindings changes are defensive and cannot be driven red (the callers already refuse a rebound or class-found binding). Five-pin cmp IDENTICAL to origin/dev; bun test 1172 pass.

CLOSURE AUDIT (2026-11-27), verified by ref on dev dd71766a: AC1 holds. The describe 'GCLI-112 — a PEP 695 type parameter shadows an enclosing binding' (test/python-hops.test.ts) carries a refused fixture per form — function, class body, type alias, bounded, constrained, TypeVarTuple, ParamSpec — plus a method of a generic class, a generic method, a nested def, a second parameter and the PEP 696 parse-error list; each asserts the receiver bin ({inRepo:0,external:0,receiver:1}) and no C.run callee, with positive twins (function, class body, type alias, a generic-class method, no type parameters). Green on dev: bun test test/python-hops.test.ts -t GCLI-112 = 33 pass, 0 fail. The five named readers were measured on dev with a scratch probe whose non-generic twin is the positive control in the same shape: 6d (x = C() once) REFUSED, twin inRepo C.run; R4 (x = C() twice) REFUSED, twin inRepo C.run; K1 (def outer(*x)) REFUSED, twin external 1; LIT (x = []) REFUSED, twin external 1; M1 (from m import inst as x) REFUSED, twin inRepo m.C.run. AC2 holds: the per-site five-pin corpus diff is recorded in all three implementation notes (delta.ts cmp IDENTICAL to origin/dev) and the handoff records byte-identical throughout; the corpus has no PEP 695 syntax, so no site moves and none is named. Caveat for a later reader: the corpus cannot exercise this change; the fixtures carry the proof. Build landed as opum-ai/glyph-cli#220 (squash 3a422ec1); GCLI-144 (02043cd3) and GCLI-146 (18b68a79) extend the same scope.
finalSummary: Closed records-only after a restore audit found the tracker still showed In Progress though the work had landed. Landed as opum-ai/glyph-cli#220 (squash 3a422ec1e599d05e1c863757b58f4556a12987a4), DEC-303 (a71)/(a72): a PEP 695 type-parameter list gets its own scope (Scope.typeParams) binding each declared name as rebound, so a read refuses instead of reaching an enclosing binding; a class body stays the first real scope for a generic declared in it, and decorators and defaults stay in the enclosing scope. Verified on dev dd71766a: the GCLI-112 describe (33 tests) passes, refused fixtures per form with receiver-bin and no-edge assertions and positive twins; the five named readers (6d, R4, K1, LIT, M1) were measured REFUSED with a resolving non-generic twin in the same shape; AC1 and AC2 checked. The per-site five-pin diff was recorded IDENTICAL to origin/dev across rounds 1-3 (the corpus has no PEP 695 syntax, so no site moves); the fixtures carry the proof. Later class-body work (#223 02043cd3, #228 18b68a79) extends the same scope.
